title: Maximum Diversity and Support Transitions on Disks and Three-Dimensional Balls
summary: For the similarity kernel $e^{-|x-y|}$, we determine the probability measure of maximum diversity on every planar disk and three-dimensional ball, answering a question of Leinster and Roff. In each dimension the measure is uniform on the boundary up to a threshold. Above it, the support is a closed central ball and the outer sphere, separated by a mass-free annulus. In dimensions two and three, their conjecture of finitely many supporting spheres therefore holds only up to the respective threshold. We obtain the measure explicitly up to one scalar root in three dimensions and through Fredholm integral equations and a scalar contact equation in the plane. Computations in dimensions four and five suggest that interior supporting spheres appear one at a time.

title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
comment: 37 pages, 14 figures; catalogue of the 338 orbits and the output of the exact checks in the appendices
summary: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.

title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
summary: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

title: The Discrete Monotonicity Property in Rank Two
summary: The Betke--Henk--Wills conjecture predicts a bound for lattice-point counts in terms of successive minima. Malikiosis introduced the discrete monotonicity property for normalized residue counts as a sufficient condition for this bound and its extension to nonsymmetric convex bodies. We prove that every compact convex set satisfies this property for lattice subgroups of rank at most two, in arbitrary ambient dimension.

title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
summary: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. More precisely, every compact connected oriented three-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary can be obtained by integral Dehn filling along a subset of the boundary components of a fundamental shadow link exterior.

title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Functor of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
summary:
We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case.
  Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. From it we also give a filtration for $π_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

title: On $κ$-covering minima
summary: We introduce $κ$-covering minima by requiring the permutation simplices of one independent lattice frame to fit into translates of a common dilate of a convex body. We prove a lower bound for their normalized product, with coefficient $(n+1)/2^n$ for centrally symmetric bodies and an explicit dependence on Minkowski asymmetry in general. On Euclidean balls, the supremum over full-rank lattices of the ratio of the resulting fitting radius to the covering radius has order $\sqrt n$. We also establish basic comparisons with classical lattice minima and bounds under products, projections, Minkowski addition, and free direct sums. We extend the definition by allowing projected periodic lattice triangulations. These extended minima agree with the classical covering minima on ellipsoids.

title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
summary: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle. At such primes dividing the quandle order, rack-space homotopy groups have exponentially many cyclic direct summands of fixed $p$-power order in each sufficiently large degree.

title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
summary: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.

title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
summary: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation. For small and large circumradius, the covering centres are constructed analytically. In the remaining range, a suitable triangle of contact points reduces the problem to a four-parameter family of ball polytopes. The parameter cube is subdivided into 23494 boxes. For each parameter box, candidate centres are found by nonlinear optimization, and the resulting covering is verified using exact rational interval arithmetic and paraboloid lifting.

title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
summary: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

title: Models of n-dimensional categories as $n\to\infty$
summary: We verify that saturated complicial sets model the right limit of the $\infty$-categories of $(\infty,n)$-categories, whereas the canonical comparison with the left limit is not an equivalence. By contrast the category of strict $ω$-categories is equivalent to both the right and left limits of the categories of strict $n$-categories.

title: The measure contraction property and rectifiability
summary: We show that a metric measure space $(X,d,\mathfrak{m})$ with finite upper $N$-density that satisfies $\mathsf{MCP}(K,N)$ is $N$-rectifiable. This removes a unique tangent requirement from arXiv:2505.01151.

title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
summary: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
summary: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

title: Lipschitz volume rigidity for non-collapsed $\rm RCD$ spaces with boundary
summary: We study Lipschitz-volume rigidity for non-collapsed ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, possibly with boundary. We prove that a measure-preserving $1$-Lipschitz map between such spaces restricts to an isometry from the interior of the domain onto its image, where the latter is equipped with the intrinsic length distance. We then characterize when this interior rigidity extends to an isometric bijection between the whole spaces, in terms of the behavior of the map on the boundaries. Along the way, we establish a rigidity result of independent interest in a more general class of rectifiable metric spaces.

title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
summary: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $Σ_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $Σ_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
summary: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrowΩΣX$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
summary: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
summary: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.

title: A short proof of the Segal conjecture for $C_p$
summary: We give a new proof of the generalized Segal conjecture for the cyclic group of prime order p, i.e. the fact that the Tate diagonal of any bounded below spectrum is a p-completion. The idea, inspired by Hahn and Wilson's argument, is to use descent along the equivariant map from the p-fold tensor power of the field with p elements to its topological Hochschild homology. The only computational input that we use is the calculation of the homotopy rings of this topological Hochschild homology and its Tate construction, together with the map induced by the cyclotomic Frobenius.

title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
summary: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

title: Higher order unknotting numbers for knots and links
comment: 18 pages; no AI tools were used at any stage
summary: Ohyama, Taniyama and Yamada showed that finite type knot invariants are insensitive to the unknotting number: for any integer n and any knot K, there is an unknotting number 1 knot which cannot be distinguished from K by any finite type invariant of order $\le n$. We generalize this result in three directions. First, we prove an analogous result for all higher order unknotting number given by $C_n$-moves. Second, we give several extensions to the link case. Third, we show that a similar result holds for ribbon 2-knots.

title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
comment: 58 pages + appendices and references. Comments are welcome!
summary:
We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra.
  The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions. When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups. Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.

title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
summary: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.

title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
summary: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.

title: Formality transmission
summary: Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences. These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc. In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission. This unifying framework allows us to extend these criteria in several directions, beyond characteristic zero and to differential graded algebras over operads or properads, leading to diverse new formality results.

title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $λ$-convex bodies
summary: For a given $λ> 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $λ$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/λ$. We show that among all $λ$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $λ$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/λ$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $λ> 0$.

title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vignéras
summary: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vignéras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

title: The Segal conjecture for large objects and semiadditive lifts
summary:
We prove a projection formula for homotopy fixed points of trivial actions of finite $p$-groups. More precisely, for every bounded-below, $p$-complete spectrum $X$ whose mod-$p$ homology is $I$-complete, the canonical map \[ (\mathbb S_p)^{BG}\otimes X \overset{\simeq}{\rightarrow} X^{BG} \] is an equivalence for every finite $p$-group $G$, where $I$ is the augmentation ideal of the Steenrod algebra.
  Building on earlier joint work with Burklund, our proof combines the Adams--Gunawardena--Miller calculation with an adaptation of Carlsson's induction. As an application, using the work of Yuan, we construct height-one semiadditive lifts of such spectra and show that their cohomology of $p$-finite spaces depends only on the $1$-type.

title: Almost Homogeneity Characterizes Almost Bi-Lipschitz Euclidean Embeddability
summary:
A metric space admits an almost bi-Lipschitz embedding into a Euclidean space if and only if it is almost homogeneous.
  We prove the sufficient direction, complementing the known necessary condition. More quantitatively, we bound the target dimension and the embedding constants for every logarithmic exponent $γ>1$. The bounds depend only on the covering parameters in the almost homogeneity condition. In particular every doubling metric space admits such an embedding. This answers a question of Margaris and Robinson and the almost bi-Lipschitz part of a question of Olson and Robinson. As a consequence, the difference set of the image is doubling, which answers the difference-set questions of Olson and Robinson and of Margaris.

title: The Torelli Group and Euler Class Zero $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Representations
summary: We prove that every representation of a closed surface group of genus at least $3$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that is sufficiently close (but not equal to) a representation that has non-compact solvable image has a simple closed separating curve that is mapped to a non-trivial elliptic element in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. This can be seen as evidence for an affirmative answer to a question of Bowditch and a conjecture of Goldman.

title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
summary: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
summary: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
summary: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth Möbius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
summary: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth Möbius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
summary: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Schütz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
summary: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Schütz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
summary: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
summary: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.
